title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
abstract: arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. Our results show: (1) more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity improves transfer to related worlds with limited gains in distant worlds, and model size improves

translated_title: 游戏中的规模化：面向多样化虚拟世界中具身智能体的持续预训练
translated_abstract: 摘要：在物理环境中，扩展数据、多样性和模型容量已经改善了具身学习，因为多样化的经验始终建立在共享的物理定律之上。然而，这些收益能否延伸到具有不同视觉风格、动态特性、控制方式和目标的虚拟世界，仍不清楚。我们通过对持续预训练（CPT）在三个维度上的受控研究来探究这一问题：数据量、多样性和模型规模。我们的120个训练配置涵盖了从0.8B到27B的四种模型规模、从50小时到1,600小时的六种数据预算，以及从仅Minecraft数据到多样化多世界语料的五种数据混合方式。我们使用三级验证损失以及从语料库内世界到未见世界的游戏玩法基准来评估性能与泛化能力。我们的结果表明：（1）更多数据可提升语料库内性能，多样性可改善向相关世界的迁移但在差异较大的世界中收益有限，而模型规模的增大可以提升……
tldr: 本文通过涵盖模型规模、数据量与数据多样性的120个训练配置，系统研究了持续预训练在多样化虚拟世界中的规模化规律，发现更多数据提升域内性能、数据多样性促进向相关世界的迁移、更大的模型规模带来性能提升。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates scaling laws for continued pre-training of embodied agents across diverse virtual worlds using 120 training configurations spanning model size, data volume, and diversity, finding that more data improves in-corpus performance, diversity enhances transfer to related worlds, and larger models yield performance gains.
